teach.title: What happened on ws-01?
teach.prompt: Read the events, decide which technique was simulated, and say which rule should have caught it before opening the answer key.
hints: Start from the unit, user and process fields; the message is free text.
A detection is only a catch if it lands after the injection started.
truth records list the attack evidence they own in `event_ids`; `side_effect_ids` are the injector's own reload lines, not the technique.

techniques.name: Sudo privilege enumeration
techniques.why: `sudo -l` asks what you are allowed to do before you do it. On a workstation that is reconnaissance, not administration.
looks_like: a sudo command line, or an auth failure
false_positives: an administrator checking their own privileges
a provisioning script that lists sudo rights

techniques.name: Transient systemd unit started
techniques.why: A transient unit has no unit file, so systemd describes it as `Started [description] ...`. That bracket is the scheduler equivalent of running from memory, and it survives a different binary asking the manager to start one.
false_positives: the same automation a user normally runs
a desktop app spawning ephemeral work

techniques.name: Ingress tool transfer
techniques.why: journald records service output, not process execution; the loopback fetch leaves no event to match.
looks_like: nothing in journald; auditd execve would be the only trace

techniques.name: Network service discovery
techniques.why: a connect sweep leaves no journal event; only the firewall's view of rejected packets is visible, and that is T1595.002.
looks_like: nothing in journald; firewall blocks are the closest signal

techniques.name: User service persistence
techniques.why: `systemctl --user enable` and `disable` write nothing, and the start line is `Starting <description>...` with the unit recorded as the manager scope. A rule would key on the attacker's own description or fire on every user service on the machine.
looks_like: Starting <description>... with the unit recorded as the manager scope

limits: Sanitized: hostnames, usernames and home paths are replaced, and every IP address is mapped into 192.0.2.0/24. Timestamps are real.
Injector-created unit names and descriptions are aliases from a fixed list; the aliasing is deterministic per scenario, so two exports of the same session agree.
The answer key is in this file. It is a scenario, not a quiz you can take blind.
Only what the exporter's providers could see is here; a technique with no telemetry appears in truth with an empty event set.
Rule text in `teach` is quoted in English even in the Portuguese export.
